![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/6f4bf1fe2f1a49f84b56702c4a83272c2f927ea4774eb677f43e525bf6cfb1f7.png)

Evaluate the triple integral 
${∭}_{R}8x\,dV$
over the region $R,$ shown above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the right one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/71f3fd0cbbde8adeca71688d6b53e2cd4cdf72076be3efa770cfebb8c10ffb76.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type III region

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le 3-\frac{3x}{4}-\frac{z}{2}\},
$$

where

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 3\}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/cd84968e9e5300a18d087ba566202aba2b7166818a590cca03eac90d4f3f7a89.png)

Hence, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 3,\,\,0\le y\le 3-\frac{3x}{4}-\frac{z}{2}\}
$$

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}8x\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{3-3x/4-z/2}8x\,dy\,dz\,dx.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{3-3x/4-z/2}8x\,dy\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{0}^{3-3x/4-z/2}8x\,dy]dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}8x[y]_{y=0}^{y=3-3x/4-z/2}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}8x(3-\frac{3x}{4}-\frac{z}{2})\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}(24x-6{x}^{2}-4xz)\,dz\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}(24x-6{x}^{2}-4xz)\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{3}(24x-6{x}^{2}-4xz)\,dz]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[24xz-6{x}^{2}z-2x{z}^{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=3}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(72x-18{x}^{2}-18x)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(54x-18{x}^{2})\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}(54x-18{x}^{2})\,dx & ={[27{x}^{2}-6{x}^{3}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =(27-6)-0 \\  & =21.\end{aligned}
$$
